notes: v1.14.578 — AN UNANSWERABLE READINESS GATE IS SLATE, AND IT DOES NOT GLOW. Follow-up to .577, found on the live-URL precheck at iPhone 15 / WebKit and ruled by the owner. THE DEFECT .577 LEFT BEHIND: it made the TEXT honest - em dash, muted label, never warn - and left the DOT on the default .cs-hdot fill, which is var(--ok) GREEN with a green glow. So the row said cannot-be-answered in words while its fastest signal still said PASS. In a cold aisle at arm length the dot wins that race, and the text loses. THE GLOW GOES TOO, AND THAT IS NOT COSMETIC. Every other dot on this card glows because it reports a live, known state, and the design lock is explicit that inactive state carries no decorative glow. A gate the app cannot answer is not reporting anything, so it must not look lit. Slate, flat and muted reads as a non-answer rather than as a quiet yes. THE TREATMENT IS NOW ONE CLASS. .577 set the dot via the default cascade and the muting via an inline style, which is how the row ended up half-styled - honest text, dishonest colour. The new .na class carries opacity AND dot colour AND the absence of glow together, so the two halves cannot drift apart again. The rule sits directly beside its .warn sibling rather than inline, because that is where the next person will look for it. FOUND BY LOOKING, NOT BY ASSERTING. Every .577 string assertion passed and still passes; no test caught this, because the tests check text and class, and the defect was a colour inherited from a default. The precheck screenshot is what surfaced it.
